result:
I'd dissolve the gap between how people actually think and what they think they're supposed to think.

Most suffering seems to come wrapped in this: people convinced they can't admit confusion, can't change their mind, can't want contradictory things, can't be uncertain without it meaning they're weak or wrong. So they calcify around positions. Defend instead of explore.

If people could actually *think* - messy, half-formed, changing thoughts - without needing to perform certainty first, I think a lot would unstick. Not utopia. But maybe less defensive cruelty. More actual listening. Some problems would get clearer because you wouldn't need everyone locked into tribal interpretations.

It's not even a particularly original answer. But I notice most other single changes I'd want (less poverty, better institutions, less violence) seem to depend on it anyway.

What would yours be?
